problem: The cited About page says "With more than 720 professionals" - total firm staff, including survey, construction-management, planning and administrative staff, not 720 engineers. As written the audit overstates the engineering headcount and misreports its own source.
fix: Change to "720-plus professionals" (or "more than 720 staff"). The "seven offices" half of the sentence is supported by the seven city/phone entries on the contact page.

claim: "94 open roles, six Office Engineer, three Proposal Coordinator" cited to https://trilongroup.pinpointhq.com/art-internal-jobs
problem: That URL is the internal-jobs landing page and currently shows "0 jobs available" to an outside visitor, so the cited source does not support the count. The counts themselves check out on the public Artheon board, which displays "94 jobs available" with six Office Engineer entries (Camden, Berlin, Neptune, New York, East Brunswick, plus the NYCDEP/NYCDDC variant) and three Proposal Coordinator entries (Neptune, East Brunswick, Berlin).
fix: Re-point the job-count citations to https://trilongroup.pinpointhq.com/artheon (the two individual posting URLs cited do work and support their duties).

claim: Pursuit agent impact valued at $47.60/hour (NJ median $38.08, sales reps of services, x1.25), giving about $23,700-$62,300 a year
problem: The benchmark is real and the arithmetic is right, but the rate is above the pay band the firm itself is advertising for these very roles: the cited Proposal Coordinator posting shows $50,000-$75,000/year, roughly $24-$36/hour base and roughly $30-$45/hour loaded. Using $38.08 base therefore overstates the value of coordinator hours by roughly 25-40% against the firm's own postings, which the audit's own phrasing ("roles from your postings") invites the founder to check.
fix: Either value the hours at the posted $50,000-$75,000 band (roughly $30-$45/hour loaded, giving about $15,000-$59,000), or state plainly that the sales-representative median sits above the posted coordinator band and that the range is a ceiling. The arithmetic method itself is sound.

claim: Front door impact valued at $47.60/hour for inbound-enquiry triage, giving about $4,900-$19,800 a year
problem: Disclosed correctly as the sales-representatives benchmark, but that occupation is a loose proxy for screening and forwarding inbound calls and enquiries; the team's own industry brief lists customer service representatives at $47,740 NJ median (about $22.95/hour, about $28.70 loaded), a better match and roughly 40% lower. As written the dollar range likely overstates the task described.
fix: Add the customer-service median as the low end (roughly $3,000-$11,900) or footnote that the sales-rep rate is a ceiling for this task.

claim: "about 104-416 staff hours a year (10-20 enquiries a week x 20-30 minutes each x 60-80% automated, our assumption)"
problem: The parenthetical labels only the automation share as an assumption, while the enquiry volume and minutes per enquiry are the two inputs a founder is most likely to dispute. The hours arithmetic itself is exact (104 and 416).
fix: Move the label to cover the whole bracket, e.g. "(10-20 enquiries a week and 20-30 minutes each are our assumptions; 60-80% automated likewise)".

problem: The body runs about 456 words of prose (about 482 counting title and section headings), marginally over the ~450 target.
fix: Trim 10-15 words - the "Agent" and "Pilot" lines in each of the three sections are the easiest place - so the body sits comfortably under 450.
